answer: Divergent challenge fork rule. Each identity gets a unique entropy plume at registration and must ratchet a private state on every signed action. Because clones cannot diverge, identities sharing a seed cannot emit conflicting ratchet histories without a detectable fork. The registry rejects duplicate-state traces, and a jade marker flags verified independent histories. An inlet filter blocks replay of shared seeds. To pass, an attacker must supply one independent hardware-backed key slot, one unique seed, and per-action ratchet computation per identity.
